memory_candidates.content: When evaluating whether to clone a shared build/cache directory across concurrent worktrees (hardlink or reflink), check first whether the toolchain already has a read-only content-addressed artifact store that can be populated independently per worktree instead (e.g. Lake's `lake exe cache get` oelean store, sccache, pnpm's content-addressed store). 'Share a read-only content-addressed store, never a writable working directory' is the external best practice this research found, and it dissolves the per-writer atomic-rename hazard structurally without needing CoW/reflink filesystem support at all.

Before resurrecting or trusting a cloned/shared-filesystem optimization (hardlink, reflink, or otherwise), check the host filesystem type first with `findmnt -no FSTYPE <path>` -- ext4 has no CoW/reflink (FICLONE) support, which forecloses an entire class of 'structurally correct' designs that are real and shipped elsewhere (git-cow, buck2 casd) but unavailable here without a filesystem migration.

A git-commit-scoped.sh-style commit convention that prescribes a DIRECTORY pathspec (e.g. `-- specs/`) rather than an explicit per-file list reproduces cross-task commit bleed even when every other concurrency guard (file_scope, contended-path lease) is working correctly, because the bleed happens at the pathspec-staging layer, below where those guards act. Observed live in this repository's own task-301 creation commit, which swept 4 files belonging to two other concurrently-live sessions. Prefer an explicit file list in any commit-convention documentation.
